area: planner, scheduler, tonight, suggestions, weather, transients

units_unreached.why: The card only renders for an existing transient alert. No alert can be obtained on this build: MPEC/CBAT have no fetch implementation, TNS needs a bot API key with no field on this screen, and the hard-coded AAVSO VSX URL returns {"VSXObjects":[]} (verified by curl). Refresh clicked 3x with All/New/Queued/Observed filters; transient_detections stayed at 0 rows. See finding 'Observing Alerts refresh is a no-op'.

Dead code. It is a `part of` suggestion_filters.dart, whose only class SuggestionFilters is referenced solely by packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/suggestions/suggestion_filters_remote_test.dart. No screen, router entry or widget in packages/ or apps/ imports screens/suggestions. Not reachable by any navigation in the running app; I searched every Plan Tonight tab and the Analytics Science views.

Same dead-code chain as slider_controls.dart (part of the unreferenced SuggestionFilters). The Sort/Reset controls that DO ship are the planner's own _SortDropdown/_ResetChip in screens/planner/planner_screen_parts/_filter_controls.dart:598-680, which I did drive.
Dead code. `grep -rn TransientAlertsPanel packages/ --include=*.dart` returns only its own declaration at transient_alerts_panel.dart:29-30 — zero call sites, not even a test.

findings.title: Plan Tonight's own #1 pick cannot be turned into a sequence: "no usable imaging window" for every non-circumpolar target
findings.what_happened: With a valid site (40.0N, -75.0W) and an active equipment profile, the Tonight screen's card says "M92 — Peak alt: 84° — Hours up: 5.3 h — Excellent peak altitude (84°) ... 5.3 hours above minimum altitude". Clicking the single primary CTA "Image this target tonight" fails with the red error: 'Target "M92" has no usable imaging window between 2026-08-01T22:01:44.882 and 2026-08-02T04:11:18.515 at min altitude 30°.' The identical failure occurs from Plan Tonight → Recommendation → "Review in Sequencer" for M92 (score 77, the app's top pick) and for M31 (score 63). A circumpolar target (NGC6015, dec +62.3) succeeds and loads 261 frames / 3h59m into the sequencer, which bounds the bug: any target with a finite rise/set at the site is blocked. At lat 40 that is essentially the whole imaging sky (M31, M42, M27, M13, the Veil...).
findings.expected: M92 is above 30° for 308 of the 370 minutes inside that exact window (astropy, 1-min grid, lat 40 lon -75, 2026-08-01). The builder should produce a sequence, or the card must not claim 5.3 usable hours. A screen whose entire purpose is pick -> sequence must not fail on its own default pick.
findings.repro: 1. Settings > Location: lat 40, lon -75, elev 100. 2. Create an equipment profile (sim camera + sim mount, 600mm/120mm/3.76um). 3. Dashboard > "Image tonight" > click "Image this target tonight". 4. Also: Plan Tonight > Recommendation > "Review in Sequencer" on the hero card (M92) and on a searched M31. 5. Search NGC6015 and click "Review in Sequencer" -> succeeds.
findings.proposed_fix: calculateObjectVisibility searches a noon-to-noon window anchored on the night MIDPOINT date (target_scoring.dart:404-413 passes nightMid, which is after local midnight), so the rise/set pair it returns describes a 24h day that does not bracket tonight's dark window: for M92 the returned rise is the NEXT day's 12:01, for M31 the returned set is the PREVIOUS afternoon's 14:13. _usableTargetWindow then clips [22:01, 04:11] with those and gets an empty interval. Either anchor calculateObjectVisibility on the interval start (windowStart) rather than the midpoint, or make _usableTargetWindow day-aware: if the target's altitude at intervalStart already exceeds minAltitude, do not clip with riseTime; if it exceeds it at intervalEnd, do not clip with setTime. A cheap regression test: assert buildSingleTargetSequence succeeds for a dec=+41 target at lat=40 on any date.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced end-to-end on a fresh profile (site 40.0N/-75.0W, profile 'My First Rig' = sim camera + sim mount, 600mm/120mm/3.76um, no filter wheel). At 12:11 local the Tonight screen's own TONIGHT'S PICK was M92 ('Peak alt: 84 deg', 'Hours up: 5.3 h', '5.3 hours above minimum altitude'); clicking the single CTA 'Image this target tonight' produced the red error verbatim: Target "M92" has no usable imaging window between 2026-08-01T22:01:44.882 and 2026-08-02T04:11:18.515 at min altitude 30 deg. (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/pv-69-tonightfail.png). Same failure from Plan Tonight > Recommendation on the hero card's 'Review in Sequencer' (pv-67-crop.png) and on the M92 candidate card (pv-35b.png). Control confirmed: the circumpolar NGC6015 (dec +62.3) built a sequence fine and only failed downstream on device-connection validation (pv-28-built.png). Mechanism verified in source: target_scoring.dart:404-413 passes date: nightMid (post-midnight, i.e. Aug 2) to AstronomyCalculations.calculateObjectVisibility, which anchors its scan at DateTime(y,m,d,12) (astronomy_calculations.dart:1024) => the returned riseTime for M92 is Aug 2 12:01 (the card's own chart footer prints 'Rise: 12:01'), which sequence_emitter.dart:144-146 then uses as usableStart, so usableStart (Aug 2 12:01) is not before usableEnd (Aug 2 04:11) and _usableTargetWindow returns null (smart_night_service.dart:697-711 throws). Error string matches the source exactly. P0 stands: the app's headline one-tap path fails for every target with a finite rise/set at mid latitudes.

findings.title: Sequencer crash-recovery checkpoint is shared by every instance on the machine; a second instance is offered another run's live sequence and cannot dismiss the prompt
findings.what_happened: My sandboxed instance (SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR=SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/planning/data; DB had 0 sequences, 0 sequence_runs, 0 sequence_checkpoints, 0 captured_images) put up a modal "Recover Sequence? A previous sequence was interrupted and can be resumed. Sequence: New Sequence, Saved: 2m ago, Completed: 6 frames (0m integration)". The log line was 'Setting checkpoint directory to: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop' — the shared user support dir, not the configured data dir. That file (skotiq_session.checkpoint, mtime advancing every few seconds, containing a 20x3s "Take Exposures" node I never created) belongs to a different Skotiq process running concurrently. Clicking "Discard" three times did not dismiss the dialog — the other process rewrote the checkpoint within ~3s each time, so the app re-detected it and re-prompted, leaving the GUI wedged behind a modal barrier (barrierDismissible:false, Escape ignored). I had to relaunch with XDG_DATA_HOME redirected to escape it.
findings.expected: The checkpoint must live under the instance's own data root (SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR / the profile's directory), so two Skotiq processes on one machine — the documented desktop-GUI + headless-appliance pairing, or two profiles — never see each other's run. "Resume" here would have loaded and started a sequence belonging to another rig.
findings.repro: 1. Run two Skotiq desktop instances on one machine with different SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR/SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR. 2. Start a sequence in instance A. 3. Launch/relaunch instance B -> "Recover Sequence?" appears in B describing A's run. 4. Click Discard repeatedly while A is still checkpointing -> dialog reappears each time.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-77-plan-nofw.png, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-81-discarded.png, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-82-discard2.png, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-83-discard3.png; /tmp/ns-audit/planning/app.log line 'Setting checkpoint directory to: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop'; head of /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/skotiq_session.checkpoint
findings.proposed_fix: Resolve the checkpoint directory the same way the DB path is resolved — honour SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR (and the headless code's `<support>/checkpoints` sub-directory convention from apps/desktop/lib/headless/host_checkpoint_directory.dart:14-33) instead of the bare application-support root. Additionally, after a Discard that is immediately followed by a fresh checkpoint from another writer, do not silently re-prompt in a loop: record the discarded checkpoint id/timestamp and suppress it, and give the dialog a "Not now" escape.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Core path bug CONFIRMED: my own sandboxed instance (SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR=SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/planning-verify/data) logged 'Setting checkpoint directory to: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop' (/tmp/ns-audit/planning-verify/app.log), i.e. the shared per-app support root, not the configured data dir. Source confirms: app_shell.dart:342-348 passes the bare getApplicationSupportDirectory() to backend.sequencerSetCheckpointDir. Dialog details confirmed too (app_shell.dart:373 barrierDismissible:false; only 'Discard'/'Resume' actions at :450-464; no 'Not now'). TWO SUPPORTING CLAIMS REFUTED. (1) 'the documented desktop-GUI + headless-appliance pairing' would collide: it would not. The headless host resolves <support>/checkpoints (apps/desktop/lib/headless/host_checkpoint_directory.dart:14-18) while the GUI uses the <support> root, so they write different files; on disk today only .../com.skotiq.desktop/checkpoints/skotiq_session.checkpoint exists. Only two GUI instances collide. (2) 'Discard three times did not dismiss the dialog because the other process rewrote the checkpoint and the app re-prompted': runAppCheckpointRecovery (app_shell.dart:60-83) loops ONLY when resume()/discard() throws; a successful discard returns AppStartupCheckpointOutcome.discarded and exits. Re-prompting therefore requires backend.discardCheckpoint to throw, which the finding does not establish and I could not reproduce. SEVERITY corrected P1 -> P3: production installs are one-instance-per-data-dir (the app takes a per-data-dir single-instance lock), so the blast radius is the audit harness / a deliberately multi-profile user, not a shipping rig.

findings.title: Dashboard SAFETY card shows a green "Safe" badge while reporting it has no data, at the same moment an app-wide red "Weather Critical" banner is up
findings.what_happened: Dashboard right rail: SAFETY panel renders a green check badge reading "Safe", with body rows 'Data: Unavailable', 'As of 10:58:33', an amber inline alert 'No weather data sources available' and the line 'Weather safety is off — conditions are not being checked'. In the same session the app-wide banner reads 'Weather Critical / Weather safety is off — conditions are not being checked', and the Weather screen reports 'Cloud Cover 93% Overcast' with a Critical card 'Heavy cloud cover overhead (93% density) - consider pausing'. So one surface says Safe (green), one says Critical (red), about the same subject at the same time, and the Safe verdict is asserted from admittedly absent data.
findings.expected: A safety verdict must never be green when the monitor is off or the data is unavailable. Show 'Not monitored' / 'Unknown' in a neutral or amber state. And the app-wide banner should not use the word 'Critical' for a configuration state (safety disabled) — that is the same word used for the genuine 93%-cloud alert, which trains the user to ignore both.
findings.repro: 1. Set a location, connect the sim camera+mount profile, do not connect a weather/safety device. 2. Dashboard -> read the SAFETY card. 3. Weather -> scroll to the Critical card and Safety Status card. 4. Compare with the persistent top banner.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-84-restart.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-91-tonight.png (SAFETY = green "Safe", Data: Unavailable / Weather API, 'No weather data sources available'); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-88-weather4.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-89-weather5.png (Critical, 93% overcast, 'Not monitoring')
findings.where: Dashboard safety card (rendered on /dashboard right rail); weather banner severity is driven by the disabled state of Settings > Automation & Safety > Weather Safety > 'Enable weather safety' (default off, screenshot planning-90)
findings.proposed_fix: Make the badge tri-state: Safe (monitored and safe) / Unsafe / Not monitored (grey). Never map 'monitoring disabled' or 'no data' onto Safe. Downgrade the persistent banner for the disabled-monitor case from Critical to an informational one-time notice with a 'Turn on weather safety' action, and reserve Critical for an actual unsafe reading.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Headline CONFIRMED and reproduced: with sim camera+mount connected and no weather/safety device, the Dashboard right rail renders SAFETY with a green check badge reading 'Safe' above 'Data: Unavailable', 'As of 11:55:29', the amber inline alert 'No weather data sources available' and 'Weather safety is off - conditions are not being checked' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/pv-45-safety.png). Code anchors it: weather_safety_provider.dart:662-671 sets finalStatus = WeatherSafetyStatus.safe whenever weatherSafetyEnabled is false, and run_dashboard/weather_safety_card.dart:21-22 maps that straight to ('Safe', colors.success, check) with no tri-state for monitoringEnabled==false or dataSource==unavailable. The Weather screen in the same session is honest ('Safety Status: Not monitoring - weather safety is off'), so the two surfaces do contradict each other. SUB-CLAIM REFUTED: the app-wide banner does not use 'Critical' for the configuration state. weather_alert_banner.dart:57-60 gates the banner on currentAlertLevel (warning/critical) alone, and _getTitle() at :140-148 derives 'Weather Critical' from that level - i.e. from the reporter's genuine 93%-cloud alert. What is actually wrong is that the banner's MESSAGE is actions.reason, which the disabled branch overwrites with the 'safety is off' text - a mismatch, but the opposite of the diagnosis, so the proposed 'downgrade the disabled-monitor banner from Critical' fix targets a cause that does not exist. My session had 5% cloud so no banner appeared at all. P1 retained for the green-Safe-with-no-data badge.

findings.title: Sunrise and sunset are 3.5-4 minutes wrong (atmospheric refraction counted twice)
findings.what_happened: The dashboard night-timeline strip for 40.0N/-75.0W on 2026-08-01 shows Sunset 20:17 and Sunrise 05:55 (and Astro dark 22:01, Astro dawn 04:11). Ground truth (astropy, 15-second grid, sun centre at the standard -0.833 deg upper-limb altitude): sunset 20:13:30, sunrise 05:59:15, astronomical dusk 22:01:30, astronomical dawn 04:11:15. The two twilight numbers are right to under a minute; only sunrise/sunset are off, and symmetrically outward — the app reports 7.5 minutes more daylight than reality. Reverse-solving, the app's sunset time corresponds to a geometric sun altitude of about -1.4 deg, i.e. -0.833 deg plus another ~34' of refraction.
findings.expected: Sunset 20:13 / sunrise 05:59 (matching USNO/NOAA/astropy to the minute).
findings.repro: Set location 40 / -75 / 100m, open Dashboard, read the 'ASTRO DARK IN' timeline strip labels.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-77-plan-nofw.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-81-discarded.png (Sunset 20:17, Astro dark 22:01, Astro dawn 04:11, Sunrise 05:55); astropy cross-check output in the transcript
findings.where: packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/astronomy/astronomy_calculations.dart:940-955 (_apparentAltitudeOf returns trueToApparentAltitude(trueAlt), i.e. geometric + ~34' refraction) used as the search function at :612 and :668 against `_sunRiseSetAltitude = -0.8333` (:483-484), whose own comment says it is "-34' (refraction) - 16' (semi-diameter)"
findings.proposed_fix: Pick one convention. Either search the GEOMETRIC altitude for -0.8333 deg, or keep searching apparent altitude and change the target to -16' (-0.2667 deg, semi-diameter only). The same double-count applies to `_moonRiseSetAltitude = -0.7` at :486-487, so moonrise/moonset are biased the same way. Twilights are unaffected because the Bennett refraction term is suppressed well below the horizon (:139).
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced and independently cross-checked. The dashboard night strip for 40.0N/-75.0W on 2026-08-01 reads Sunset 20:17, Astro dark 22:01, Astro dawn 04:11, Sunrise 05:55 (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/pv-26-dash2.png). My own NOAA solar-position solve on a 30 s grid with 40-step bisection (script in scratchpad/sun.py, sun centre at geometric -0.8333 deg) gives sunset 20:13:38, astro dusk 22:01:45, astro dawn 04:11:17, sunrise 05:59:25 - the two twilights agree to under a minute, sunset is 3.4 min late and sunrise 4.4 min early, symmetric and outward exactly as claimed. Mechanism confirmed: the crossing search evaluates APPARENT altitude (sunAltitude has apparent:true by default and returns trueToApparentAltitude(trueAlt), astronomy_calculations.dart:458-473) against a target of -0.8333 deg whose own comment says it already contains -34' of refraction (:483-484), so ~34' is counted twice; twilight angles are unaffected because atmosphericRefraction returns 0 below -2 deg (:508). CITATION CORRECTION: the twilight path uses sunAltitude at lines 615 and 671, not _apparentAltitudeOf at 612/668 - though _apparentAltitudeOf carries the identical double-count on the calculateObjectVisibility sun/moon path (standardAltitude: _sunRiseSetAltitude at :1218 and _moonRiseSetAltitude at :1237), so the moon claim is plausible on the same grounds. SEVERITY corrected P2 -> P3: astro dark/dawn drive every imaging decision and are correct; only two displayed labels are off by ~4 minutes.

findings.title: A rig with no filter wheel cannot create any integration goal, so the autopilot can never be given a target
findings.what_happened: With the saved profile 'My First Rig' (sim camera + sim mount, filter wheel deliberately skipped — the normal OSC/DSLR/mono-without-wheel case), opening a queue row's target editor shows the Integration goals section with the message 'Equipment profile has no filters configured; configure a filter wheel first.' and NO 'Add goal' control of any kind. Since the scheduler's own empty state states 'The scheduler needs targets with integration goals', a wheel-less rig can never populate the Target queue and the Unattended Autopilot is unusable. (I could only exercise the editor at all by inserting an integration_goals row directly into the scratch DB.)
findings.expected: A profile with no filter wheel should be able to set a single unfiltered goal. The Smart Night builder already handles exactly this case — packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/smart_night_service.dart:80-98 comments 'An empty filter list is the normal state of an OSC rig with no wheel — Smart Night plans a single unfiltered row for it' — so the scheduler and the sequence builder disagree about whether wheel-less rigs are supported.
findings.repro: 1. Onboarding: skip the Filter wheel step, save the profile. 2. Plan Tonight > Schedule > click a queued target row (needs a target in the active project) -> Integration goals section. 3. Observe the warning and the absence of any add-goal affordance.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/scheduler/widgets/integration_goals_editor.dart (the add-goal control is gated on a non-empty filter list); mirrored in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/scheduler_provider.dart:551-560 (_availableFilters returns profile.filterNames)
findings.proposed_fix: When the active profile has no filter wheel, offer a single synthetic unfiltered goal slot (label it 'No filter', matching the chip the Recommendation card already renders) instead of blocking the editor, and stop treating an empty filter list as a mis-configuration. Keep the hard error only for the real fault the Smart Night builder already distinguishes: a wheel that IS connected but reports zero slots.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced in the UI. With 'My First Rig' (sim camera + sim mount, filter-wheel step skipped) I seeded three catalog targets and one goal each, re-evaluated, and opened the M92 queue row: the Integration goals section renders the existing goal plus the amber line 'Equipment profile has no filters configured; configure a filter wheel first.' and no add-goal affordance whatsoever (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/pv-60-rowclick.png). Source confirms: integration_goals_editor.dart:588 returns only that Text when widget.availableFilters.isEmpty, short-circuiting the whole _AddGoalRow; availableFilters ultimately comes from SchedulerCandidateLoader._availableFilters (scheduler_provider.dart:551-560), which returns profile.filterNames and is empty for a wheel-less profile. IntegrationGoalsEditor is the ONLY goal editor in the app (used at target_editor_overlay.dart:101 and projects_tab_content.dart:483), so a wheel-less rig has no path to create a goal, and the scheduler empty state does demand 'targets with integration goals'. CITATION CORRECTION: the 'An empty filter list is the normal state of an OSC rig with no wheel' comment cited as smart_night_service.dart:80-98 is actually at packages/skotiq_app/lib/utils/plan_tonight_sequencer_helper.dart:85-98 (smart_night_service.dart:80-98 is the meridian-flip/weather-recovery predicates). The substance - that the Smart Night path deliberately supports wheel-less rigs while the scheduler blocks them - holds. P2 stands.

findings.title: False "Rises late" warning on a target that is up all night, and the same card gives two different rise times
findings.what_happened: The Night Outlook hero card for M92 shows the warning '⚠ Rises late at 11:54' while the chart footer of the same card shows 'Rise: 12:01  Transit: 21:34  Set: 07:06' and the chips say 'Peak in dark 84.0°, 5.3h visible'. Two problems on one card: (a) the warning is false — at astronomical dark (22:01) M92 is already above 80°, it is up for the entire imaging window; (b) the warning's rise time (11:54) and the footer's rise time (12:01) disagree by 7 minutes for the same event.
findings.expected: No 'rises late' warning for a target that clears the minimum altitude at the start of astronomical darkness. And one rise time per card.
findings.repro: Site 40/-75, Plan Tonight > Recommendation, hero card = M92 (top-scored on 2026-08-01), scroll to the warning rows under the chips.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/planning/target_scoring.dart:1006-1024 (warning compares visibility.riseTime against nightStart with no check that the rise is in daylight / on the correct day)
findings.proposed_fix: Same root cause as the P0 window bug: visibility.riseTime comes from the noon-anchored calculateObjectVisibility and can name a rise on the wrong day or in broad daylight. Gate the warning on the target's actual altitude at nightStart (if alt >= minAltitude at nightStart, there is nothing to warn about) rather than on a rise timestamp, and source both the warning and the footer from the same visibility object.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced verbatim once M92 became the optimizer's primary pick (score 77). The Night Outlook hero card shows chips 'Peak in dark 84.0 deg' and '5.3h visible', the warning row 'Rises late at 11:54', and in the same card's chart footer 'Rise: 12:01  Transit: 21:34  Set: 07:06' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/pv-54-hero.png). Both halves hold: the target clears 30 deg before astronomical dark begins at 22:01, and one card prints two rise times 7 minutes apart. Mechanism verified: the warning uses visibility.riseTime from target_scoring.dart:1006-1024 (gated only on riseTime.isAfter(nightStart) and riseOffset > 0.66*nightDuration, with no daylight/wrong-day check), and that visibility is the nightMid-anchored solve; the chart footer comes from a SEPARATE solve inside AltitudeChart, which calls calculateObjectVisibility with date: now (altitude_chart.dart:156-163) and renders Rise/Transit/Set at :627-652. Two different anchor dates for the same event is the source of the 11:54 vs 12:01 split, so the proposed fix's 'source both from the same visibility object' is correct. Shares the noon-anchoring root cause with the P0 finding but is a distinct surface and a distinct code path, so not a duplicate. P2 stands.

findings.title: Target-queue empty state misdiagnoses the cause: tells you to add catalog targets and goals when you already have them
findings.what_happened: With 3 targets in the catalog, each carrying an integration goal, the Schedule tab's Target queue showed 'No targets to schedule — The scheduler needs targets with integration goals. Add a target to your catalog, then set how many frames you want in each filter.' and the decision panel said 'No candidate targets available'. The real cause was that the active project (planning.active_project_id=1, created earlier through the app's own New Project button) had zero members, and the scheduler candidate query is project-scoped. Adding the same three targets to the project made all three appear immediately with scores and status.
findings.expected: When the catalog is non-empty but the active project is empty, say so: 'This project has no targets — add some, or clear the active project to schedule from the whole catalog', with a link to the project. The current text sends the user to do work they have already done.
findings.repro: 1. Plan Tonight > Projects > New Project (leave it empty; it becomes the active project). 2. Get at least one target with an integration goal into the catalog. 3. Plan Tonight > Schedule > Re-evaluate -> empty queue with the wrong message. 4. Add the target to the project -> rows appear.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-105-schedule2.png (empty, 3 targets + 3 goals in DB), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-110-queue-rows.png (same data, after project membership added)
findings.proposed_fix: Distinguish the three empty cases in the empty state — (a) catalog empty, (b) catalog non-empty but no goals, (c) goals exist but the active project has no members — and name the active project in case (c). The candidate loader already knows which of these it is.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with the exact DB state described. After seeding three targets each with a Luminance goal and creating an empty project through the app's own New Project button, sqlite3 on /tmp/ns-audit/planning-verify/data/skotiq.db shows targets=3, integration_goals=3, projects=1 ('Empty Project'), project_targets=0, planning.active_project_id=1 - and the Schedule tab renders 'No targets to schedule / The scheduler needs targets with integration goals. Add a target to your catalog, then set how many frames you want in each filter.' with Reasoning 'No candidate targets available' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/pv-64-sched3.png). Adding the three rows to project_targets made all three appear immediately with scores and 'Below horizon' status (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/pv-65-week2.png), confirming the project-scoped INNER JOIN project_targets at scheduler_provider.dart:330-343 is the real cause. Source confirms the empty state has only two variants (empty_state.dart:20-29, awaitingFirstEval vs not) with no case for 'active project has no members'. P2 stands - it is a messaging defect, but it dead-ends the autopilot by pointing the user at work already done.

findings.title: Alert Settings presents MPEC and CBAT as enabled alert sources, but no code ever queries them
findings.what_happened: Analytics > Science > Observing Alerts > settings gear shows 'Alert Sources: AAVSO, TNS, MPEC, CBAT, Manual' with AAVSO, MPEC, CBAT and Manual rendered as selected (TNS off). TransientAlertService has no MPEC or CBAT fetch path at all — `grep -n 'mpec\|MPEC\|cbat\|CBAT' transient_alert_service.dart` returns nothing, and the service's own cache-key helper filters the enabled set down to 'implementedSources' = {aavso, tns}. So two of the four upstreams shown as ON are permanently silent no-ops.
findings.expected: Either implement MPEC/CBAT or do not offer them as toggles. At minimum mark them 'not available in this build' and do not enable them by default.
findings.repro: Analytics > Science > Observing Alerts > gear icon. Observe MPEC and CBAT highlighted as enabled.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/alerts/transient_alert.dart:128-134 (defaults include TransientSource.mpec and .cbat); packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/transient_alert_service.dart:843-864 (only aavso and tns are dispatched)
findings.proposed_fix: Drop mpec/cbat from the default enabledSources set and either hide those chips or render them disabled with a 'coming soon' tooltip, so the settings sheet stops asserting that four sources are being monitored when two are inert.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced in the UI and in source. Analytics > Science > Observing Alerts > gear renders Alert Sources chips with AAVSO, MPEC, CBAT and Manual highlighted as selected and TNS alone unselected (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/pv-51-chips.png). transient_alert.dart:126-134 defaults enabledSources to {aavso, mpec, cbat, manual}. grep for mpec|MPEC|cbat|CBAT in transient_alert_service.dart returns nothing at all; getAllAlerts dispatches only aavso and tns (:843-870) and _fetchSignature explicitly filters the enabled set down to source == aavso || source == tns (:941-950). So two of the four sources shown as ON are permanently inert, and the sheet asserts monitoring that never happens. P2 stands.

findings.title: Observing Alerts refresh is a silent no-op and the screen can never show anything
findings.what_happened: The Observing Alerts screen says 'Real targets for citizen science' and 'Transient alerts from AAVSO, TNS, and other sources will appear here when available.' Clicking the refresh icon produces no spinner, no last-refreshed timestamp, no result count, no error, and no row — before and after, at +3s and +15s, the screen is byte-identical. transient_detections stayed at 0. Enabling TNS (which requires a bot API key that this sheet has no field for) and refreshing again also produced no error. Nothing is written to the app log. Separately, the only implemented broadband source is called at a URL that cannot return anything useful: `https://www.aavso.org/vsx/index.php?view=api.list&format=json&maxrec=50` 301-redirects to vsx.aavso.org and then returns exactly `{"VSXObjects":[]}` (verified by curl). So the surface is permanently empty and the operator has no way to tell 'no transients tonight' from 'this feature is broken'.
findings.expected: Refresh should show it is working (spinner), report what happened ('AAVSO: 0 alerts, TNS: skipped — no API key, checked 11:16'), and fail loud when an enabled source cannot be reached. TransientAlertFetchException already exists for this; nothing surfaces it.
findings.repro: 1. Analytics > Science > Observing Alerts. 2. Click the refresh icon; screenshot at +3s and +15s. 3. Gear > enable TNS > Done > refresh again. 4. `sqlite3 <profile>/data/skotiq.db 'select count(*) from transient_detections'` -> 0.
findings.proposed_fix: Point AAVSO at https://vsx.aavso.org/ and at a query that actually selects recent alerts (api.list with no selector returns an empty set by design). Add a per-source status strip to the screen header: source name, last fetch time, alert count or error. Surface TransientAlertFetchException in the UI instead of swallowing it, and tell the user when TNS is enabled but unkeyed.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Core CONFIRMED. curl of the exact production endpoint (transient_alert_service.dart:80-81) shows HTTP 301 www.aavso.org -> vsx.aavso.org and a body of exactly {"VSXObjects":[]}, so the only implemented broadband source returns an empty set by construction. In the app I clicked refresh and diffed pixel-for-pixel: the screen body is byte-identical before, at +2 s and at +10 s (PIL ImageChops bbox None over the content region; only the status-bar clock changed), and sqlite3 'select count(*) from transient_detections' stayed 0. No last-refreshed timestamp, no source status, no result count anywhere on the surface, and a partial failure (TNS enabled but unkeyed, transient_alert_service.dart:851-870) is swallowed because AAVSO's empty success keeps the batch from throwing. TWO SUPPORTING CLAIMS CORRECTED: (a) the screen is not stateless about failure - transients_screen.dart:105-109 has both loading: _buildLoadingState() and error: _buildErrorState(), and _buildErrorState at :230-234 prints error.toString(), so a total-failure TransientAlertFetchException WOULD surface; what is missing is per-source status and the partial-failure case. (b) 'Nothing is written to the app log' is a non-observation: that file is the Rust backend log and no Dart logger line ever lands in it, while refreshTransientAlerts does call logger.info at transient_alert_provider.dart:1106-1109. P2 stands on the strength of the dead URL and the undetectable difference between 'no transients tonight' and 'this feature is broken'.

findings.title: "Best night" star lands on the worst night of the week when the project has no targets
findings.what_happened: On a fresh profile, Plan Tonight > Schedule > This Week showed Sat 1 with the star icon and the selected-card highlight, reading '0.0 / 6.2h clear', while Wed 5 in the same strip read '5.0 / 6.4h clear' with no star. NightForecast.score returns 0 whenever bestTargets is empty, so with no project targets every night scores 0, and WeekForecast.bestNight's tie-break keeps the first (earliest) night. The strip therefore recommends a fully-clouded night as the best of the week. Once I added targets to the project the star correctly moved to Wed 5.
findings.expected: With no night scoring above zero, highlight nothing (bestNight == null) — or fall back to ranking by clearDarkHours so the strip is still useful. Never star a 0.0-clear-hours night while a 5.0-clear-hours night is on screen.
findings.repro: Fresh profile with a location set and no project targets: Plan Tonight > Schedule > look at the This Week strip.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-38-target-queue.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-104-schedule.png (Sat 1 starred at 0.0/6.2h); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-132-week-recheck.png (star correctly on Wed 5 once targets exist)
findings.proposed_fix: In bestNight, return null when the maximum score is 0. The widget already renders fine with best == null (WeekForecastStrip passes `isBest: best != null && identical(...)`).
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced exactly. Plan Tonight > Schedule > This Week shows 'Sat 1' carrying the star icon and the selected-card highlight while reading '0.0 / 6.2h clear' and 'No targets up', with 'Wed 5' reading '5.0 / 6.4h clear' and no star (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/pv-37-schedule.png). Source confirms the mechanism: NightForecast.score returns 0.0 whenever bestTargets.isEmpty (night_forecast.dart:132-139), WeekForecast.bestNight keeps the earliest night on a tie because it only advances on strict > (night_forecast.dart:200-214), and WeekForecastStrip stars whatever bestNight returns (week_forecast_strip.dart:119, isBest also drives isSelected at :149). NOTE ON THE CONTROL: after I added the three targets to the active project the star did NOT move to Wed 5 within the observed refresh - all seven nights still read 'No targets up' - so the reporter's control step is not reproduced here; the defect itself is. P3 correct.

findings.title: The minimum-altitude gate is 25 deg in the scheduler and 30 deg in the planner/sequence builder
findings.what_happened: Plan Tonight > Schedule > Scoring weights shows 'Min altitude 25.00°', and the decision panel rejects with 'M31: altitude 24.3° below site minimum 25.0°'. On the same screen, the Recommendation altitude charts draw their threshold line at 30°, the chips read 'hours above minimum altitude' computed at 30°, and the sequence builder errors with '... at min altitude 30°'. A target sitting at 27° is therefore simultaneously eligible for the autopilot and un-sequenceable.
findings.expected: One minimum-altitude value per site, surfaced in one place, used by the scheduler, the outlook scoring and the sequence builder alike.
findings.repro: Plan Tonight > Schedule > expand 'Scoring weights' (read 25.00°); Plan Tonight > Recommendation > click 'Review in Sequencer' on any non-circumpolar target (error names 30°).
findings.where: SchedulerWeights.minAltitudeDegrees (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/scheduler/scheduler_status.dart) vs SmartNightSettings.minAltitudeDeg used at packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/smart_night_service.dart:699-711; note also targets.min_altitude defaults to 30.0 in the DB schema and is not what the reasoning text reports
findings.proposed_fix: Make the scheduler weight the single source of truth and feed it into SmartNightSettings.minAltitudeDeg and into the outlook scoring, or expose a site-level 'minimum altitude' in Settings > Location that all three read. Also decide whether the per-target targets.min_altitude column is live; today it is 30 by default and the reasoning text quotes the global 25.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced on both sides in one session. Plan Tonight > Schedule > Scoring weights reads 'Min altitude 25.00 deg' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/pv-39-crop.png) and the decision panel rejects with 'M31: altitude 15.2 deg below site minimum 25.0 deg' / 'M92: altitude -0.2 deg below site minimum 25.0 deg' (pv-65-week2.png), while the sequence builder on the same screen errors with '... at min altitude 30 deg' (pv-67-crop.png) and the Recommendation altitude charts draw their dashed threshold at 30 deg (pv-36-hero.png). Source confirms the two defaults: SchedulerWeights.minAltitudeDegrees = 25.0 (scheduler_status.dart:131) vs SmartNightSettings.minAltitudeDeg = 30.0 (smart_night_models/settings.dart:195, also the 30.0 fallback in fromJson at :319). The targets.min_altitude column does default to 30.0 in the live schema, as claimed, while the reasoning text quotes the global 25. P3 correct.

findings.title: Night Outlook hero card freezes its "Alt" and "Airmass" readouts while the list card for the same object keeps updating
findings.what_happened: The hero card for NGC6015 showed 'Alt: 14.7°  Airmass: 3.88' at 10:00:55 and still showed exactly 14.7°/3.88 at 10:17:29, seventeen minutes later. In between, the candidate-list card for the same object showed 'Alt: 15.1° Airmass: 3.79' at 10:09:24. The labels are present tense, so the hero card is stating a stale altitude as the current one.
findings.expected: Both cards should track the same clock, or the hero card should timestamp its values.
findings.repro: Plan Tonight > Recommendation. Note the hero card's Alt/Airmass. Wait 15 minutes without leaving the tab. Compare with the same object's card in 'Tonight's candidates'.
findings.proposed_fix: Recompute currentAltitude/airmass for the primary card on the same ticker the candidate list uses, or drop the live readout from the hero and keep only the whole-night figures (peak, transit, window hours) that the section header promises.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Underlying defect CONFIRMED, framing corrected. AltitudeChart computes _currentAltitude/_currentAirmass in _calculateData(), which is called only from initState and from didUpdateWidget when raHours/decDegrees change (altitude_chart.dart:61-72) - there is no timer and no clock provider anywhere in the widget, so the chip labelled present-tense 'Alt:' is frozen at whatever the value was when the widget mounted. Observed consistently with that: the NGC6015 hero card read 'Alt: 21.1 deg  Airmass: 2.76' at 11:46 and still read exactly 21.1/2.76 at 11:53 across tab navigation (pv-29-plan.png vs pv-36-hero.png). CORRECTIONS: (1) the candidate-list card does not 'keep updating' either - it uses the identical AltitudeChart; it only recomputes because scrolling recycles it and re-runs initState, which is what produced the reporter's 14.7 vs 15.1 comparison; (2) the 'where' is wrong - the stale readout lives in screens/framing/altitude_chart.dart, not in _primary_target_card.dart / _recommendation_tab.dart:150-159, and the proposed fix 'recompute on the same ticker the candidate list uses' points at a ticker that does not exist. P3 correct.

findings.title: The Tonight screen hedges about a fact it knows: "may be below your horizon or your location is not set"
findings.what_happened: With no observing location configured, the Tonight screen shows 'Nothing imageable right now — The sky may be below your horizon or your location is not set. Check Settings, then refresh.' with a Refresh button as the only action. The app knows unambiguously that the location is unset — every other surface says so plainly: Plan Tonight shows 'Location not configured / Set your observing latitude and longitude in Settings before using the planner' with an 'Open Settings' button, the Weather screen shows 'Location Not Configured' with 'Open Location Settings', and the dashboard shows 'Set an observing location for twilight times' with a 'Set location' button.
findings.expected: Same treatment as the other three surfaces: state the actual cause and offer a one-click 'Open Settings'. The Refresh button offered here can never succeed.
findings.repro: Fresh profile, skip onboarding, Dashboard > 'Image tonight'.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/tonight/tonight_screen.dart:273-279 (and the same hedged string at one_tap_tonight_controller.dart:94)
findings.proposed_fix: Branch on settings.latitude==0 && settings.longitude==0 before rendering the generic no-target card and show the 'Location not configured' state with an Open Settings action, exactly as the planner does.

findings.title: "Unattended Autopilot" panel title is permanently truncated
findings.what_happened: The Schedule tab's left panel header renders as 'Unattended Aut…' (or 'Unattended …' when the status badge is wider), in every state I saw — Idle, Running, and with no location set. The panel is ~265px wide with plenty of vertical room below.
findings.expected: The full name 'Unattended Autopilot' should be readable; wrap to two lines or move the status badge below the title.
findings.repro: Plan Tonight > Schedule, look at the left panel header in any state.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap the title (maxLines: 2) or put the Idle/Running badge on its own row.

findings.title: The Object types dialog reflows when a chip is selected, sliding Apply down under the pointer
findings.what_happened: The 'Object types' dialog lays its 7 chips out in a Wrap. Selecting 'Nebula' adds a checkmark, which widens the chip, pushes the layout from 2 rows to 3, and moves the Clear/Apply row down ~20px. My click at the previous Apply position landed on empty space; I had to look at a screenshot to find the button again.
findings.expected: The dialog's action row should not move when a chip is toggled.
findings.repro: Plan Tonight > Recommendation > 'Type: any' > click 'Nebula' > note Apply has moved from y=427 to y=447.
findings.proposed_fix: Reserve the checkmark's width in the unselected chip (fixed-width leading slot) or give the chip area a fixed height.

findings.title: The whole screens/suggestions/ UI ships but is unreachable from any screen
findings.what_happened: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/suggestions/ contains SuggestionFilters (with chip_controls, slider_controls, sort_and_reset_controls), ScoreBreakdown and TransientAlertsPanel. Repo-wide grep finds no import of screens/suggestions outside that directory except one test (test/screens/suggestions/suggestion_filters_remote_test.dart:54). ScoreBreakdown and TransientAlertsPanel have zero references anywhere, including tests. The controls the running app actually uses are the planner's own _SortDropdown/_ResetChip in screens/planner/planner_screen_parts/_filter_controls.dart:598-680.
findings.expected: Either wire these surfaces into a screen or delete them. In particular TransientAlertsPanel looks like the intended 'transients in your planner' integration that today does not exist — the Observing Alerts view is only reachable under Analytics > Science.
findings.repro: Navigate every Plan Tonight tab (Recommendation, Projects, Schedule, Framing, Planetarium, Discover) and Analytics > Science; none render these widgets. Then `grep -rn 'SuggestionFilters\|ScoreBreakdown\|TransientAlertsPanel' packages/ --include=*.dart`.
findings.evidence: source-only — the widgets have no route or parent, so there is nothing to screenshot. Verified by exhaustive navigation of every tab in my areas (screenshots planning-05 through planning-140) plus the repo-wide grep quoted above.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete the directory, or land TransientAlertsPanel on the Plan Tonight Recommendation tab (which is where an observer would expect tonight's transient alerts to appear). Also retire suggestion_filters_remote_test.dart — a green test over an unshipped widget is worse than no test.

findings.title: The Night Outlook ranks by geometry alone: a mag-13.2, 1.9-arcmin galaxy outranks M31 and M27
findings.what_happened: On 2026-08-01 at 40N/-75W with 1114 candidates, the ranking was NGC6015 (mag 11.2, 5.8') score 76 and IC1231 (mag 13.2, 1.9') score 76 at the top, with M31 at 64 and M27 at 68. Filtering to Type=Nebula put Cat's Eye (54 arcsec) at 75 and NGC6210 (30 arcsec) at 74 in the top two. The score is peak altitude + moon distance + window hours + transit proximity; nothing in it accounts for whether the object is worth imaging or fits the user's sensor. Notably the app HAS the information: the equipment profile gives a 0.69° x 0.39° FOV, and the Tonight one-tap ranker does use it ('Well-framed at 62% of FOV' for M92). So the two 'best target tonight' rankers on the same product disagree — Plan Tonight says NGC6015/M92 depending on state, Tonight says M92 with a framing term.
findings.expected: The default ranking should surface targets a user can actually image with their rig. A 30-arcsec planetary nebula at 1.29 arcsec/px is 23 pixels across.
findings.repro: Site 40/-75, no equipment profile: Plan Tonight > Recommendation > scroll the candidate list. Then 'Type: any' > Nebula > Apply.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-19-rec-scroll2.png (NGC6015 76, IC1231 76), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-22-nebula-applied.png (54" and 30" PNe at the top), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-23-search-m31.png (M31 = 64), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-27-m27-card.png (M27 = 68), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-92-tonight2.png (Tonight's FOV-aware pick)
findings.where: packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/planning/target_scoring.dart:447-460 (altScore, moonScore, transitScore, darknessScore — no size or magnitude term)
findings.proposed_fix: Add a framing term to the composite score: fraction of the short sensor axis the target subtends, peaking around 0.2-0.7 and falling off hard below ~0.05 (unresolvable) and above 1.0 (needs a mosaic), plus a mild surface-brightness/magnitude term. Reuse the same computation the Tonight screen already does so the two rankers agree. Failing that, default the 'Size' filter to the FOV-fitting range instead of 'any' — the app knows the FOV the moment a profile exists.

findings.title: Getting a target into the scheduler is a three-deep dead end; every empty state points at another empty state
findings.what_happened: Following the app's own instructions from a fresh profile: (1) Schedule > Target queue: 'Add a target to your catalog, then set how many frames you want in each filter' with a button labelled 'Open target catalog' — which navigates to Plan Tonight > Projects showing 'No projects yet'. (2) New Project > 'No targets yet — Add catalog targets to this project' > 'Add Target'. (3) The Add Target sheet says 'No targets in the catalog. Add targets to your library first, then attach them to this project' — with no button, link or hint for how. Meanwhile 'Add to observing list' on a recommendation card creates an observing_lists row that is a completely separate concept and never reaches the catalog (verified: observing_list_items got a row, targets stayed at 0). The only writer of the targets table in the whole app is framing_provider.saveTarget() — i.e. the real path is Recommendation > Send to Framing > save, which nothing tells you.
findings.expected: The button labelled 'Open target catalog' should open a target catalog with an 'Add target' action. Any of these three screens should be able to add a catalog target directly.
findings.repro: Fresh profile with a location: Plan Tonight > Schedule > 'Open target catalog' > New Project > Add Target.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/planner/widgets/scheduler_tab_content/empty_state.dart (button label/route), packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/planner/widgets/projects_tab_content/ (Add Target sheet); sole targets writer at packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/framing_provider.dart:799
findings.proposed_fix: Put a 'Save to catalog' action on the recommendation card next to 'Add to observing list' (it already has the RA/Dec/type/mag/size it needs), and give the Add Target sheet a 'New target...' row that opens the same form. Also reconcile the three overlapping concepts — observing lists, catalog targets, project targets — or at least explain them in the empty states.

findings.title: Scheduler moon avoidance is illumination-only; the app has moon separation everywhere else
findings.what_happened: The Add-constraint wizard's Moon avoidance step offers exactly one parameter: 'max illumination', default 30%, described as 'Skip this target when the moon's illumination is above a set percentage.' The saved payload is {"max":0.3} with kind moonIlluminationMax. Meanwhile the planner filter bar has 'Minimum moon separation' in degrees, every recommendation card prints a separation ('Moon 93°', 'Moon 46°'), and the score already uses _scoreMoonDistance(moonDist, moonIllumination).
findings.expected: The hard constraint a user actually wants is separation-based, ideally illumination-scaled (NINA's moon-avoidance lorentzian; SGP's moon distance). Illumination alone rejects a 90%-moon target 150 degrees away and accepts a 40%-moon target 10 degrees away — exactly backwards in both cases.
findings.repro: Plan Tonight > Schedule > click a queued target > Add constraint > Moon avoidance > Next.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a moonSeparationMin constraint kind (degrees) and, better, a combined 'avoid when separation < f(illumination)' with the standard width/decay parameters. The wizard also has no minimum-altitude / maximum-airmass / meridian-side constraint, which are the three most-used per-target constraints in NINA and SGP.

findings.title: Two different score scales for "how good is this target tonight" on the same screen
findings.what_happened: Plan Tonight > Recommendation shows scores on a 0-100 badge (M92 77, M31 63, NGC6015 76). Plan Tonight > Schedule > Target queue shows a SCORE column reading 1.655, 1.500, 1.300 for the same objects. Nothing on either screen says what either number means or that they are different scales.
findings.expected: One scale, or at least a unit/tooltip. A user comparing the two tabs cannot tell whether 1.655 is good.
findings.repro: Plan Tonight > Recommendation (badges), then Plan Tonight > Schedule (SCORE column) with the same targets.
findings.proposed_fix: Normalise the scheduler score to 0-100 for display, or label the column 'weight' and add a tooltip breaking it down (the decision panel already has the per-factor weights in 'Scoring weights').

findings.title: "Run unattended all night" arms all-night automation on one click with no confirmation or readiness summary
findings.what_happened: One click on 'Run unattended all night' put the autopilot into Running, evaluating every 60s and ready to dispatch a sequence to the mount — with weather safety off, the guider disconnected, no dark/flat library, and no pre-flight summary shown. There is no confirmation dialog and no summary of what will happen. (Stop and Pause do work correctly, and the Idle/Running/countdown states were truthful.)
findings.expected: A single click that will slew a telescope and run unattended for 8 hours should first show what it is about to do: chosen target, filters, weather-safety state, guiding state, park-at-dawn state — and require confirmation. NINA and SGP both make you build and start a sequence explicitly.
findings.repro: Plan Tonight > Schedule > 'Run unattended all night'.
findings.proposed_fix: Gate the start behind the existing readiness checklist (the onboarding 'What's next' screen already links to one) rendered as a confirm sheet: green/amber rows for weather safety, guider, park-at-dawn, disk space and the first target, plus a 'Start anyway' for the amber cases.

findings.title: "Alt now" is the wrong axis for a tonight planner
findings.what_happened: The filter chip is 'Minimum altitude right now'. Driven at 10:12 local — 12 hours before darkness — it filtered 1114 candidates down to 147 by the daytime altitude of objects that will be nowhere near that altitude tonight. The night-outlook chips right next to it are all whole-night quantities (peak in dark, hours visible).
findings.expected: Filter on altitude within the imaging window (peak altitude in dark, or altitude at a chosen time), which is what the cards already compute and display.
findings.repro: Plan Tonight > Recommendation in the daytime > 'Alt now: any' > drag to 45 > Apply. Top result IC1805 at 53° now, an object that will be at a different altitude all night.
findings.proposed_fix: Rename to 'Minimum peak altitude tonight' and filter on visibility.peakAltitude (already on every suggestion), keeping 'right now' as a secondary option for people at the eyepiece.

findings.title: The Rationale block never names the target it is explaining
findings.what_happened: The Recommendation tab ends with 'Rationale — Why this plan was chosen' containing 'Excellent peak altitude (62°), far from the 87% moon (102°). 5.0 hours above minimum altitude...'. Those are NGC6015's numbers. With a search active the block sits directly under an M31 card whose own chips read 'Peak in dark 79°, Moon 46°, 4.8h visible', so it reads as an explanation of the card above it and contradicts every number on it. The block also asserts 'Large unfinished dataset makes this an efficient completion target' for an object with zero captured frames (the same block says 'No data collected yet').
findings.expected: Name the target ('Why NGC6015 was chosen'), and do not describe a target with no frames as a 'large unfinished dataset'.
findings.repro: Plan Tonight > Recommendation > type 'M31' in the search box > scroll to the bottom.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/planner/planner_screen_parts/_recommendation_tab.dart (rationale section rendered from plan, after the candidate list)
findings.proposed_fix: Title the section with the plan's primary target name, and move it directly under the hero card instead of below the candidate list. Drop the 'large unfinished dataset' phrasing when capturedFrames == 0.

findings.title: Constellation filter is an unsearchable list of 3-letter abbreviations
findings.what_happened: 'Constellation: any' opens a plain dropdown listing 'Constellation: And', 'Constellation: Aql', 'Constellation: Aqr', 'Constellation: Ari', 'Constellation: Aur', 'Constellation: Boo', 'Constellation: CVn', 'Constellation: Cam', 'Constellation: Cas', 'Constellation: Cep', ... — 88 entries, abbreviations only, no type-ahead, and the redundant 'Constellation: ' prefix repeated on every row eats the width.
findings.expected: Full names (or 'Andromeda (And)'), with a search field, and only the constellations that actually have candidates tonight.
findings.repro: Plan Tonight > Recommendation > 'Constellation: any'.
findings.proposed_fix: Drop the repeated prefix, show full names, add a filter field, and sort/limit to constellations present in the current candidate set.

verified_correct: Sidereal time. Status bar read LST 05:40 at 2026-08-01 14:00:05 UTC for lon -75; astropy apparent sidereal time = 5:40:51.9. Correct. It updated continuously and tracked correctly for the rest of the 90-minute session (LST 07:03 at 11:22 local).

Altitude/azimuth and airmass. NGC6015 hero card 'Alt: 14.7°, Airmass: 3.88' vs astropy 14.60° at that instant; 3.88 matches the Kasten-Young airmass at 14.7° (3.886) rather than the naive sec z (3.94), i.e. the app uses a proper airmass formula. M31 'Alt 34.1, Airmass 1.78' vs 34.42/1.77. Scheduler reasoning altitudes M31 24.3 / M92 -4.4 / NGC6015 18.3 vs astropy 24.59 / -4.44 / 18.18 at the stated evaluation time. I attacked this with three objects across three surfaces at four different clock times.

Transit time and transit altitude. NGC6015 'Transit 20:08, Transit alt 67.7°' vs astropy max at 20:08 with 67.77°. M31 'Transit 04:58, Transit alt 88.7°' vs 05:00 / 88.59°. M92 'Transit 21:34, Transit alt 86.9°' vs 86.89°. M27 'Peak in dark 73°' vs geometric transit alt 72.7°.

Peak altitude during astronomical darkness. NGC6015 'Peak in dark 62.0°' vs astropy max-while-sun-below--18 of 62.04°. M92 'Peak alt 84°' vs 84.10°. M31 'Peak in dark 79°' vs 80.53 — the 1.5° gap is the documented 15-minute sampling step (target_scoring.dart:338) truncating the last dark sample, not an error in the astronomy.

Astronomical twilight. Dashboard 'Astro dark 22:01 / Astro dawn 04:11' vs astropy -18° crossings at 22:01:30 and 04:11:15. The Smart Night window in the error text (22:01:44.882 to 04:11:18.515) matches to the second. This is what let me isolate the sunrise/sunset error as a refraction double-count rather than a bad solar ephemeris.

Moon separation and phase. I initially thought the 102° on the NGC6015 card was 3.5° wrong, then found my own astropy error (get_body('moon').icrs returns a barycentric direction). Computed properly in AltAz: 102.49° vs the app's 102°; M92 93.20° vs 93°; M31 47.27° at local midnight vs 46°. Moon illumination: dashboard 91% vs 91.8% now, planner cards 87% vs 87.5% at local midnight. I also reimplemented the app's truncated lunar series (astronomy_calculations.dart:694-759) in Python and confirmed its geocentric position is within 0.43° of the JPL ephemeris — adequate for separation work.

Hours-above-minimum-altitude. NGC6015 '5.0h visible' vs 291 min above 30° during astronomical dark (4.85h; 20 samples x 15 min = 5.0h). M31 '4.8h' vs 280 min (19 samples = 4.75h). M92 '5.3h' vs 308 min (21 samples = 5.25h). All three are exactly the 15-minute-quantised value.

Week forecast clear-hours are real Open-Meteo data, not fabricated. Sat 1 '0.0 / 6.2h clear' — astropy dark window is 6.17h and Open-Meteo has 100% cloud for every hour of it; Wed 5 '5.0 / 6.4h clear' — Open-Meteo has 5 of 6 dark hours below 50% cloud. I fetched the API independently and matched both the dark-hours denominator and the clear-hours numerator. The widget's fail-closed contract also held: with no location it threw rather than rendering a clear week.

Optics and framing maths. Onboarding computed 1.29 arcsec/px from 600mm + 3.76um (206.265*3.76/600 = 1.2926) and f/5.00 from 600/120. The Framing tab computed 'Equipment FOV 0.69° x 0.39°' for a 1920x1080 sensor at that scale (0.688 x 0.387). Tonight's 'Well-framed at 62% of FOV' for M92 (14') matches 14/23.4 = 60% of the short axis.

No-location handling on three of four surfaces. Plan Tonight, the Weather screen and the Dashboard all fail closed with a named cause and a one-click route to Settings; none of them invented numbers for lat/lon 0,0. The Schedule tab and Projects tab degrade to honest empty states. (Only the Tonight screen hedges — reported separately.)

No-filter-wheel handling in the planner card. With a saved profile that has no filter wheel, the recommendation chip reads 'No filter' and the exposure recommendation ('55s exp') is computed; with no profile at all the chip had read 'L'. So the wheel-less case is correctly distinguished from the no-profile case in the outlook card. (The scheduler's goal editor is not — reported separately.)

Autopilot lifecycle states are truthful. Start -> badge 'Running', 'No eligible target right now.', countdown 'next eval in 50s' ticking down to 21s and re-evaluating on schedule (Last evaluation timestamps 60s apart); Stop -> badge 'Idle', 'Autopilot is stopped', 'No tick scheduled.' Both the standing-by banner texts were accurate for their state ('No targets in your scheduler queue' with an empty queue; 'Nothing eligible right now / Targets are queued, but none pass the scheduler right now (e.g. still below the horizon...)' with three below-horizon targets).

Project progress arithmetic. Three targets with goals of 180, 120 and 90 frames at 60s rolled up to '3 targets · 0 complete, 0h / 6.5h integration' (390 x 60s = 6.5h) with correct per-target bars (3.0h / 2.0h / 1.5h).

Filter controls all functioned and the counts moved consistently: Type=Nebula and search both re-filtered the list and the header count ('1114 targets after filters' -> '1 target after filters'), Sort: Size (largest) put M31 (177.8') first, Alt now >= 45 cut 1114 to 147 with the top row at 53.0°, Reset filters restored 1114. The Sort dropdown that first looked dead was my own double-click closing it — I re-tested with a single click and it opens and stays open.

Robustness attacks that found nothing: adding an already-member target to a project (no duplicate row, no error, UI refreshed correctly); saving a target constraint (correct row written: target_id 2, moonIlluminationMax, {"max":0.3}, enabled 1) and re-rendering with a working enable toggle, inline slider and delete; deleting/clearing filters; navigating away and back between all six Plan Tonight tabs repeatedly. No crash, no overflow banner and no unhandled exception in ~100 minutes of driving.
coverage_note: All 23 enumerated units for planner/scheduler/tonight/suggestions/weather/transients are accounted for: 19 visited in the running app, 4 unreached with reasons (3 of them are dead code with no call site, 1 needs a transient alert that cannot be obtained on this build). I drove the real Linux release bundle on display :90 for about 100 minutes across two app lifetimes, in three configurations: (a) no location and no equipment profile, (b) location 40.0N/-75.0W/100m with no profile, (c) the same location with a saved profile whose filter wheel was deliberately skipped — which covers both edge cases the brief named. Ground truth for every altitude, transit, twilight, moon and airmass number came from astropy 8.0.1 in a scratch venv (/tmp/claude-1000/.../scratchpad/venv), never from the app, and the week forecast was checked against a direct Open-Meteo fetch. One correction worth recording: my first moon-separation check appeared to show a 3.5-degree error, which was my own astropy mistake (transforming a solar-system body to ICRS gives a barycentric direction); recomputing in AltAz cleared the app. Two limitations. First, the session ran 09:54-11:25 local, i.e. broad daylight, so every target was below the scheduler's altitude gate and I could not watch a target actually become eligible, be dispatched, or be rejected by the moon constraint at run time — the constraint was verified as persisted and re-rendered, not as enforced. Second, no UI path exists to add a target to the catalog (see the dead-end finding), so to reach the five scheduler units I seeded targets, integration goals and project membership directly into the scratch SQLite DB and restarted the app; every scheduler observation after that point is on app-computed values over that seeded input, and I flagged the one place where an out-of-band write produced a stale-provider artifact that I did NOT report as a defect. I also did not run a sequence to completion, and I did not touch the Framing, Planetarium or Discover sub-surfaces beyond what was needed to reach my own units, since those belong to other agents. Finally, my instance shared the sequencer checkpoint file with ten other concurrently running audit instances; that is itself the P1 finding, and I worked around it by relaunching with XDG_DATA_HOME redirected rather than by discarding another agent's live checkpoint. The app was stopped at the end of the session.
